Organization 1: ACAT Canada URL: https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/acatcanada/
Website: http://acatcanada.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details Chemin
de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine, Montreal QC H3T1B6 514-890-6169 Social networks Mission
Christian Action for the abolition of torture (ACAT) is the Canadian branch of an international
federation, FIACAT, having consultative status at the UN. ACAT Canada is a national ecumenical

organization that has been defending human rights for nearly 40 years. It intervenes especially in
cases torture and the death penalty. It informs through awareness and action campaigns,
intervenes through letters of protest from its members to the authorities concerned, educates to
human rights, invites spiritual reflection and above all, ensures that situations are reported to the
UN of mistreatment still existing in Canada. Its head office is in Montreal and its activities are take

place in French, but it has members across Canada. Description Pleas, Human rights education,
Spirituality, Support for healing victims of torture

Organization 3: Corporation of Master Electricians of Quebec URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/corporation-des-maitres-electriciens-du-quebec/
Website: https://www.cmeq.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5925
boulevard Décarie, Montréal QC H3W 3C9 Toll-free: 1 800 361-9061 514 738-2192 Hours of
Operation SCHEDULE Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 1:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Mission The mission of the Corporation of Masters Électriciens du Québec (CMEQ) is to protect the
public by verifying the qualification, probity and competence of its members. It regulates and
disciplines the professional conduct of electrical contractors, providing security and expertise to the
community. Description Corporation of Master Electricians of Quebec About the CMEQ Since 1950,
the Corporation of Master Electricians of Quebec (CMEQ) protects the public by verifying and

controlling the qualification of its members to guarantee their integrity and competence. It regulates
and disciplines the professional conduct of electrical contractors. Services offered Verification of the
qualification of members Regulations and professional discipline Information on electrical safety
laws and practices Continuing education for electrical contractors General public The CMEQ
protects the public by verifying the qualifications of its members and providing information on

electrical safety laws and practices. Electrical contractors The CMEQ develops practical tools and
technical, legal and information documents administrative to support its members in their practice of
the profession. Services offered to entrepreneurs Tools and calculators Reference documents
Partnerships with Hydro-Québec and other Training specific to the operation of a subcategory 16
license Continuing training The CMEQ offers a range of training for electrical contractors, adapted

to the operation of a subcategory 16 license, as well as general training useful for management of a
construction company. Center of expertise and training (CEF) The CEF of the CMEQ offers a portal
for members to access training and declare their working hours. continuing education. Respondents
carrying out construction work must follow 16 hours of training over a 24-month period. Types of
training available Administration and business management Code, standards and regulations

Contracts, legal obligations and responsibilities Occupational health and safety Production
techniques For more information, contact the CMEQ at 514 738-2184 (option 7) or by email at
formation@cmeq.org.

Organization 4: Support URL: https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/lacteurnational/
Website: http://lpeut.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 400, boul. de
Maisonneuve O., office 720, Montréal QC H3A 1L4 514-789-2460, ext. 188 Opening hours
SCHEDULE The Service Caregiver Info is open 7 days a week, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Social
networks Mission La mission of Support for caregivers is to contribute to the support of loved ones

caregivers who provide unpaid care and support to people around them. As part of this mission,
Support offers the Helper Info service. For further information on the organization and the
Info-aidant service, visit lentreprises.org. Description Founded in 2009, Support for caregivers is a
non-profit organization funded by the Government of Quebec and the Lucie and André Chagnon
Family. The main mandate of the Support for caregivers consists of supporting the deployment of

information services, training, psychosocial support and respite, through funding from organizations
present in the areas. L’Appui also acts as an agent of mobilization and consultation of the various
actors who dedicated to supporting caregivers and helping to improve their quality of life. This
mission is carried out nationally, but also thanks to a presence in 17 deployed regions throughout
Quebec, as well as a specific development agreement for Terres-Cries-de-la-Baie-James.

Organization 6: The Quebec Black League URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/la-ligue-des-noirs-du-quebec/ Website:
https://liguedesnoirs.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5201
boulevard Décarie, Montréal QC H3W 3C2 514 489-3830 514 489-2843 Opening hours
SCHEDULE Monday to Friday 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Mission The mission of the Quebec Black
League is to defend the rights of person, to fight against injustice and discrimination, and to offer

support to people victims of racism and racial profiling. We are committed to promoting equality of
chances and opportunities for all citizens, by raising awareness among governments and society to
the importance of respecting fundamental rights. Description The Negro League of Quebec The
Quebec Black League is a non-profit organization founded in 1969 to defend human rights and
social justice. We are at the service of all cultural communities who struggle to obtain impartial

justice, covering not only the Quebec but all of Canada. Our Services Defense of human rights daily
for the black and cultural community. Legal clinic offering services free. Youth Integration Project to
help young people aged 16 to 30 integrate into the labor market. The Black League of Quebec is
the only organization to offer a service on human rights daily to people from the black and cultural
community. We We are here to help you if you are a victim of racism, discrimination, or any other

injustice. About Us The Quebec Black League works to raise moral awareness, social, political and
economic of Canada. We denounce injustices and discrimination of the vicious system by being the
spokesperson for the voiceless, the oppressed and the victims. If your rights have been violated or
violated, do not hesitate to contact us. Our goals include defense of community rights, popular
education for respect for the rights of citizens, raising awareness among governments of the

importance of equal opportunities, encouraging citizen participation, and the defense of victims of
injustice and abuse of power. Since 1969, The League of Blacks of Quebec has established links
with other organizations to better serve the community. We refer certain complaints to the
appropriate authorities and have created specialized organizations to meet specific community
needs.

Organization 7: Elizabeth Fry Society of Quebec - SEFQ URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/societeelizabethfryduquebec/ Website:
http://elizabethfry.qc.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5105, Chemin
de la Côte Saint-Antoine, Montreal QC H4A 1N8 514-489-2116 514-489-2598 Opening hours
SCHEDULE Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Mission The Elizabeth Fry Society of Quebec

is an organization community founded in 1977. Its mission is to help women who have in trouble
with the law, who have already had them or who are at risk of having them. She ensures
compliance with rights of women as well as the improvement of their conditions of detention.
Description The values that support our action are: accountability, respect for oneself and others,
autonomy, affirmation and honesty. We aim to: promote the social integration of women brought to

justice, in a supportive and supervisory environment; meet their needs by offering them specialized
services adapted to their economic and social situations; defend their interests and raise
awareness among governments and public opinion of their reality; raise awareness different
community resources to their needs in order to maximize the services available to them. are
offered.
